messages:
sara: Anyone else seeing a 20-40ms micro-hiccup in prod when prefix KV cache warms? Started ~09:12 UTC, affects short-chat small-batch requests.

matt: Yep, saw the same on canary — p95 up ~30ms for seq<=64. Feels like something flips mid-request.

kai: I pulled traces. Profiler shows a spike in memcpy + kernel launch overhead around the switchover point to the fused-flash variant. Example from perf dump:

```
# timeline (us)
0.0  start_request
1.2  lookup_kv_cache
2.0  choose_kernel -> fused_flash_v2
2.4  cudaMemcpyAsync (kv->gpu)  18000us
22.6  kernel_launch (fused_flash_v2) 45us
22.7  kv_apply  2us
```

Looks like the memcpy batch grows at the same time we choose fused, causing a higher launch path.

oliver: Which commit changed kernel selection heuristics? I can bisect if you point me.

matt: I added some lightweight timestamps from the kernel chooser yesterday. Raw log snippet:

```
[09:11:58] chooser: eval_features={batch=2,seq=32,kv_size=16}
[09:11:58] chooser: score_fused=0.73 score_paged=0.27 -> select=fused
[09:12:03] request_end
[09:12:03] next_req chooser: kv_warmed=true -> allow_switch=true
```

infra-bot: deploybot: canary rolled back at 09:25 due to latency bump :warning:

sara: Proposed bisect plan: start at commit abc2f4 then abc2f9 range where batching heuristics changed. @oliver can you run a quick bisect with the repro (small local run)? I can repro locally.

oliver: On it. Reproducer command I'm using:

```
./tools/run_repro --model=gptj --seq=64 --batch=2 --warm_prefix=16 --profile --iterations=100
```

oliver: Quick update — bisect points to commit abc2f7 which toggled `prefers_fused_for_small_batches=true`. Reverting that locally removes the micro-hiccup. p50 unchanged, p95 back down ~32ms.

kai: That makes sense. Fused-flash has lower steady-state token cost but higher setup overhead when KV entries are non-trivial. The selector is switching mid-session once kv_warmed flips. Suggestion: avoid kernel swaps mid-request; only change kernel at request boundary or when kv_warmed==false.

sara: Agreed. Patch suggestion: add a per-request `sticky_kernel` flag so once a kernel is chosen for a request we don't switch until next request. Also emit a new metric `kernel_switchover_ms` and a counter `kernel_switch_count` to track frequency.

matt: :thumbsup: I'll draft the PR and add a bench in bench-suite covering warmup transitions and small-batch cases. Test will assert no >10ms spike on swap path.

eva: If we roll the fix to canary, let's set a 30m observation window and guard with automatic rollback on p95 regression >10ms. Also add route-level monitoring since this hits only short-chat routes.

infra-bot: alert: perf-monitor p95 spike count=17 in 09:12-09:27 window; canary was reverted.

sara: Thanks all — I'll open the follow-up issue with repro steps, bisect result (abc2f7), logs, and assign @matt for the PR. Will also add the new metrics to observability dashboards.

matt: I'll include the metric names in the PR description so ops can wire alerts.

oliver: PR test ran locally, patch candidate improves p95 by ~28ms on repro. Pushing draft in a few minutes.

sara: Great. Once draft is up we'll run canary and watch tail for 1h.

(ended)
